title: Pre-public security review of ward-cli at b1dae53 (operator request via opum-doc)
description: The operator asked first-party, through opum-doc, for a pre-public security review of Ward at origin/dev b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d, relayed by team-lead 2026-10-29. Three read-only Opus reviewer units (detached worktrees review-sec-a, review-sec-b, review-sec-c under .claude/worktrees/ at that SHA) each return a verdict by message; this task records the three verdicts. The repository visibility flip is tier 3 and the operator alone; nothing here changes visibility.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The verdict of each of the three reviewer units is recorded on this task, naming the reviewed SHA and the unit
Every finding is dispositioned: filed as its own task, or recorded as not-a-defect with the reason

implementationNotes:
VERDICTS, recorded 2026-10-30 from the team-lead relay. Reviewed SHA for all three: b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d. Units: ward-cli-review-sec-a, -b, -c, read-only, detached worktrees. Model: claude-opus-5-5 for each, reported by the leader as verified MATCH with spawn-model (not re-measured here). Full texts for a and c are in the leader scratchpad (wardsec/verdict-sec-a.txt and verdict-sec-c.txt).

(a) SECRET CUSTODY: READY-FOR-PUBLIC. No finding above LOW. LOW-1 leftover typed or pasted bytes reach the shell (passphrase reader truncates instead of refusing; neither reader flushes the tty). LOW-2 a backup passphrase has no minimum (design choice, A/B to opum-doc). LOW-3 a reporting.ts comment states a false custody invariant and every vault read turns all secret values into immutable strings. LOW-4 ward restore creates a key without taking setup.lock. LOW-5 race between creating a backup file and stripping its inherited ACL. INFO-1 zeroing incomplete in several copies. INFO-2 chmod -N gets the path without --. INFO-3 files Ward did not create keep an inherited ACL. INFO-4 no secure_delete pragma. INFO-5 install runbook trains remember-this-choice without checking the dialog names the binary. Conceded and documented, not new: ward backup is gated only by stdin.isTTY, the key is readable through the trusted build, rollback is undetected, same-user TOCTOU on ~/.ward.

(b) APPROVAL AND TRANSPORT: FIX-BEFORE-PUBLIC. Headlines as the leader relayed them: the DEC-248 secret-header gap (being fixed in opum-ai/ward-cli#208); a new spoofable approval prompt; an agent can approve its own profile through a pseudo-terminal, which the spec concedes but the README does not say. NOTE: verdict-sec-b.txt in the scratchpad holds only transcript residue and the leader summary, not the unit full finding list, so the per-finding detail for (b) is NOT recorded here and must be supplied before AC2 can disposition it.

(c) PUBLIC EXPOSURE: FIX-BEFORE-PUBLIC. 1 CRITICAL fork pull requests reach the self-hosted runners (ci.yml on pull_request, all jobs on self-hosted Linux ARM64); the leader measured allows_public_repositories=false on the Default and mbpm2 runner groups, so a fork PR would get no runner and not execute, but every PR to dev would then block on required checks that never report. 2 MEDIUM GitHub-held refs (206 refs/pull/N/head) are permanent on the flip, a history rewrite does not remove them. 3 MEDIUM personal data and local machine facts in history and tree (author email and name, local username and home paths in hook-written notes and .quest records). 4 LOW internal infrastructure detail (runner group and pod names, ruleset id, RUNNER_HOST in the release notes). 5 LOW internal process material and private product names, including the WCLI-84 alias and Vercel bypass mechanism. 6 LOW release install proves integrity not authenticity (suggests build-provenance attestation). 7 LOW README and runbook go stale on the flip. 8 INFO no LICENSE and no SECURITY.md. All 23 secret-scanner hits triaged as not real credentials (code naming a secret, an eval canary, throwaway test TLS keys under test/fixtures/tls, expected to need a scanner allowlist).

AC2 stays open: dispositions follow opum-doc ruling and the operator A/B. No fix task is filed here.
